name: Fathom
verdict: Self-serve: create an app at fathom.video/marketplace_applications/new and each user authorizes their own account, likely in 1-3 days. The docs say apps are subject to review but do not say it blocks installs.
needGuide: Short one: create the app, add HTTPS redirect URIs, and build the authorization link with the Fathom SDK.

auth.detail: Two methods. API keys are per user, sent as `X-Api-Key`, with no org-level keys. OAuth apps use authorization code, token URL https://api.fathom.ai/external/v1/oauth2/token, a single scope `public_api`, and a Bearer token. Access tokens are short-lived. Refresh tokens are single-use and rotate on each refresh. PKCE is not mentioned.

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days (no review documented); review timing unknown

approval.gate: No hard gate documented. OAuth apps are 'subject to review to ensure the best experience for all users', but the docs do not say review blocks installs. Marketplace/co-marketing promotion is quarterly and invites apps with 20+ users. Production redirect URIs must be HTTPS, and multiple production URIs need separate OAuth apps.

scopes.why: One scope (public_api) with full API access for the authorizing user.
scopes.summary: Only `public_api` (full Fathom API access for the authorizing user). No per-resource scopes, so no scope-triggered review is documented.

cost: Free; API access is included on all plans
prerequisites: Account and owner: Any developer with a Fathom account can register an app (eligibility not stated). Use a company-owned account because the app is tied to the registering user.
Where you register: Fathom marketplace applications → New: set redirect URIs and receive Client ID and Client Secret (docs say about 2 minutes).
Cost: Free; API access is included on all plans

registerAt.path: Fathom marketplace applications → New: set redirect URIs and receive Client ID and Client Secret (docs say about 2 minutes).

steps.do: Sign in to Fathom and open fathom.video/marketplace_applications/new.
Create the app: set HTTPS redirect URIs (several allowed for dev, one per production app) and save the Client ID and Secret.
Build the authorization link with the Fathom SDK (getAuthorizationUrl / get_authorization_url, scope public_api, state).
Exchange the code at the token URL with grant_type=authorization_code, then persist tokens in a real TokenStore.
Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token, store the new refresh token each time and serialize refreshes with a lock.
Call /recordings summary and transcript endpoints (OAuth cannot use include_summary or include_transcript on /meetings).
Review Fathom brand guidelines and email help@fathom.video about listing or launch materials.

roles.team: Any developer with a Fathom account can register an app (eligibility not stated). Use a company-owned account because the app is tied to the registering user.
roles.customer: The individual Fathom user authorizes their own account. Tokens see meetings they recorded or that were shared with them or their team; private calls stay host-only even for Admins. Admin controls blocking OAuth apps are not documented.

testing: Use your own Fathom account (API keys work on all plans) and register multiple development redirect URIs.
Token endpoint limit is 60 requests per 60 seconds per OAuth app.

blockers.problem: Refresh tokens are single-use, so concurrent refreshes fail with HTTP 400
blockers.fix: Lock per connection and store the new token.

blockers.problem: OAuth apps cannot use include_summary/include_transcript on /meetings
One production redirect URI per app
blockers.fix: Register separate apps per environment or domain.

blockers.problem: Review process and timing are undocumented

automation.agentCan: Write the OAuth flow with the SDK, implement locked refresh, run test calls to meetings, summary and transcript, draft launch copy and brand-compliant listing text.
automation.humanMust: Log in to Fathom to register the app, authorize the test account, and handle any marketplace or partner contact with Fathom.

uncertain: Who may register apps, whether review blocks customer installs, PKCE support, access-token lifetime, authorization endpoint URL, and MCP auth (api.fathom.ai/mcp) details were not documented in fetched pages.
